column1: # tools/doom/core-unreached.tsv — fields no shipped configuration writes, and why.
# A field listed here is declared by the schema and written by the original
# only under a gate that no shipped program opens: its configuration. The
# owner approved this table on 2026-09-17 (the trace configuration). On
# 2026-10-21 the owner chose job mode 0 for the native program (decision
# 0008), which makes the job list and its executor -- job modes 1 and 2,
# tools/doom/emit-schema.rb carries each row into state.tsv as an `#unreached`
# line. tools/doom/audit-core.rb requires every output or persistent field that
# step or render code writes to have a CORE writer -- a migrated definition
# writing it outside the gates listed here -- unless this table names it.
# tools/doom/migration-ledger.rb reads the configuration names from here.
# `gates` names the definitions whose gated code writes the field (or calls
# WHAT A ROW CLAIMS: no shipped program produces the field's data. Four rows
# claim it in a narrower form, and their reason begins RESET ONLY: the frame's
# counter is set to 0 on a shipped path (render_player_view) and every read of
# it is gated, so nothing shipped ever sees a value other than the reset.
# tools/doom/audit-core.rb checks both halves of that for any listed field it
# finds written on a shipped path.
